Captured from the local application · 12 October 2026

From source data to a reviewed energy metric

An energy analyst needs one reusable answer: What is the measured electricity consumption? Build its meaning, verify its calculation, then release a version that queries can trust.

Target definition: imported kWh from VALID, non-estimated readings, across the available sample period.

Captured result: 8,547.282 kWh · Release: walkthrough-v1 · Runtime: typed local DuckDB.

Source tables + business note → GPT-4o candidate → editable Studio draft
                                                          ↓
Query result ← activate ← publish ← reviewed version ← SQL validation + item review

Follow along: use your existing instance on port 8084. Screenshots use a separate instance on port 8085 with the same application.

The walkthrough's approval records use an explicit automation identity for synthetic demonstration only. Your original draft and versions remain unchanged.

Open your StudioInspect the completed demo

Where each task belongs

SectionResponsibility
Semantic StudioInspect sources, generate and edit drafts, validate SQL, and review individual changes.
Semantic HubApprove complete versions, compare, publish, inspect artifacts, and choose the active version.
Data queryExecute predefined reviewed metrics and inspect their result and evidence.

This guide contains 19 actual screenshots. Images are embedded, so this HTML file works offline. Local app links require a running instance.

01

Data query

Start with the business question

  1. Open http://localhost:8084/demo to follow along in your own workspace.
  2. Ask: What is the measured electricity consumption?
  3. Check the context status before running a query.
What you should see

The starter snapshot awaits review. Run example stays disabled until a reviewed context becomes active.

You are defining a reusable metric for an energy analyst. Include valid, non-estimated readings only; report kWh.

02

Semantic Studio → Source data

Inspect the actual source fields

  1. Open Semantic Studio, then select Source data.
  2. Select meter_readings and inspect its columns and sample rows.
  3. Find import_kwh, quality_status, is_estimated, and meter_id. Inspect meters to understand the source relationship.
What you should see

Typed fields and up to ten sample rows appear. The source relationship links readings to meters.

The selected power pack has four tables. This walkthrough uses synthetic source data and the available reporting period.

03

Context artifacts → Attach documentation to draft

Give the builder business evidence

  1. Expand Attach documentation to draft and choose power-business-notes.md from this guide's folder.
  2. Enter table meters, column meter_id, and entity value SYN-M000.
  3. Select Attach to draft. Save any unsaved edits first.
What you should see

The saved revision increases. The document receives a content hash and a verified source-entity link.

The note explains valid, non-estimated kWh. The link identifies an example meter; it does not filter the metric to that meter.

Business note to upload
# Measured electricity consumption

This document describes a synthetic demonstration dataset.
Count imported energy only when quality_status is VALID and is_estimated is false.
The unit is kWh. Reporting dates use Asia/Singapore. This demonstration has no date filter.
Owner: Energy Analytics. Meter SYN-M000 is an example source entity.
This note records intended meaning; the SQL expression must enforce the conditions.
04

Semantic Studio → Source data

Generate a candidate, then inspect it

  1. Select Generate with LLM and wait for the candidate.
  2. Expand Provenance, Source evidence, Assumptions, and Warnings.
  3. Check the measured_import_kwh formula and its evidence before selecting Apply to draft.
What you should see

Provenance records OpenAI and gpt-4o. Generation alone leaves the draft unchanged; Apply to draft creates the next revision.

GPT output can vary. Create evidence draft is the deterministic alternative. Extra suggested metrics require their own business review.

05

Semantic Studio → Studio

Inspect the semantic model visually

  1. Inspect the table chain: substations, feeders, meters, and meter_readings.
  2. Select measured_import_kwh in the object tree or canvas.
  3. Keep this walkthrough focused on that metric. Remove any unrelated generated suggestions from this draft.
What you should see

The inspector shows the selected metric. The canvas distinguishes source relationships from SQL-derived dependencies.

Moving nodes changes the saved layout, not the semantic definition. Connections and metric edits change the draft.

06

Metric inspector → Business meaning and evidence

Record business meaning and ownership

  1. Expand Business meaning and evidence. Set Owner to Energy Analytics.
  2. Add Measured electricity consumption and Verified imported energy as separate synonym lines.
  3. Record valid readings as the inclusion rule and estimated readings as the exclusion rule. Save draft.
What you should see

Business metadata becomes part of the saved context. The metric retains kWh units and its conditional SUM expression.

Descriptions explain rules. SQL must enforce them. This example uses CASE conditions; it needs no additional structured filters.

07

Validation & review

Understand the validation gate

  1. Select Validation & review, then Validate SQL.
  2. Inspect the message when independent reference SQL is missing.
  3. Return to Studio to supply the missing evidence.
What you should see

Validation requests reviewer-authored reference SQL. Complete-version approval remains blocked.

This screenshot intentionally demonstrates the gate. Once you understand it, add the reference before your first validation.

08

Studio → Metric inspector

Write an independent calculation

  1. Find Independent reference SQL for measured_import_kwh.
  2. Paste the reference query below, after checking its conditions against the business definition.
  3. Select Save draft.
What you should see

The reference uses WHERE conditions. The semantic expression uses CASE conditions; both represent the same chosen business rules.

Keep the output alias measured_import_kwh. The reference must come from your business understanding, not an LLM-generated expected answer.

SELECT SUM(import_kwh) AS measured_import_kwh
FROM meter_readings
WHERE quality_status = 'VALID'
  AND is_estimated = 'false';
09

Validation & review

Compare SQL results and relationship checks

  1. Select Validate SQL again.
  2. Compare compiled SQL, reference SQL, and both result sets.
  3. Check the relationship results for duplicate keys, null target keys, and unmatched rows.
What you should see

All checks pass for saved revision 4 in this capture. Both calculations return 8,547.282 kWh.

Revision numbers can differ in your session. Agreement proves this sample reconciliation; the reviewer still confirms business meaning.

10

Validation & review → Definition review

Review exactly what changed

  1. Keep Starter definitions as the comparison baseline.
  2. Find measured_import_kwh and expand Before / after.
  3. Inspect highlighted metadata and SQL changes. Clear the filter before reviewing the remaining objects.
What you should see

The comparison highlights changed fields. This walkthrough has 24 review objects, including document evidence and ontology mappings.

Inspect metrics, relationships, metadata, documents, and mappings. A technical pass does not approve these business decisions.

11

Validation & review → Batch decision

Approve an inspected group of objects

  1. Inspect the remaining objects, then clear Find objects to include them all.
  2. Select all matching, then Approve selected.
  3. Check eligible and blocked counts. Enter your reviewer name and note, confirm the checkbox, then confirm the decision.
What you should see

All selected eligible items receive decisions for the exact saved revision. Blocked items stay unresolved.

Use Request changes when an item is unclear. These screenshots use an automation reviewer only in the separate synthetic walkthrough workspace.

12

Semantic Hub

Create an immutable reviewed version

  1. Open Semantic Hub after every required item is approved.
  2. Enter walkthrough-v1 as the version name, or another unused name.
  3. Enter your reviewer name and review note, confirm the checkbox, then select Approve whole version.
What you should see

The version freezes its definition, semantic model, validation evidence, review decisions, and context artifacts.

The button stays disabled if validation is missing, outdated, or unsuccessful, or if required item decisions remain unresolved.

13

Semantic Hub → Version history

Inspect the version before publication

  1. Find walkthrough-v1 in Version history.
  2. Select Inspect to examine its immutable context and validation evidence.
  3. Use Download context JSON if you need the complete reviewed package.
What you should see

The version is Reviewed · unpublished. Use for queries is still disabled.

Approving a version does not publish it. The current query context remains unchanged.

14

Semantic Hub → Version history

Publish, then activate deliberately

  1. Select Publish for walkthrough-v1 and confirm local publication.
  2. Check that the version now shows Published.
  3. Select Use for queries. Check that the button changes to Active for queries.
What you should see

The active context becomes walkthrough-v1. A newly opened query page receives this version and its context hash.

Publication makes the version available locally. Activation chooses which published version the local query page uses.

15

Context artifacts

Inspect the complete version package

  1. Choose walkthrough-v1 in Inspect version.
  2. Select Inspect artifacts and expand semantic layer, metadata, ontology, documents, and quality.
  3. Check that the uploaded note, its entity link, and metric metadata belong to this version.
What you should see

The panel returns the frozen artifacts from the reviewed version. Draft inspection instead loads the latest saved draft.

Ontology mappings remain structural proposals with separate review evidence. Documents remain supporting assertions, not automatically authoritative facts.

16

Semantic Hub → Version history

Compare a release with its baseline

  1. Choose walkthrough-v1 under Compare version.
  2. Choose Starter definitions under Baseline and select Compare versions.
  3. Expand the metric or another changed object to inspect its before/after fields.
What you should see

The version comparison identifies changes without modifying either version.

Use the same controls to compare two reviewed versions when a later release exists.

17

Data query

Run the approved metric

  1. Open Data query after activating the version.
  2. Confirm the active context is walkthrough-v1.
  3. Choose What is the measured electricity consumption? and select Run example.
What you should see

The result is 8,547.282 kWh for this synthetic source snapshot.

The query page currently runs predefined reviewed metrics. GPT-4o generated the authoring proposal; it does not plan this query.

18

Data query → Execution evidence

Trace the answer to its definition

  1. Expand Execution evidence below the result.
  2. Inspect the compiled SQL and its VALID/non-estimated conditions.
  3. Check the context version, source snapshot, SQL hash, and result hash.
What you should see

The displayed answer is tied to the active semantic context and the selected source snapshot.

The business story is complete: a supported definition became a reviewed version and then a traceable result.

19

Semantic Hub → Create draft

Start the next revision safely

  1. Return to Semantic Hub and select Create draft on walkthrough-v1.
  2. Make the next business change in Studio and save it.
  3. Validate, review, approve a new version, publish, and activate when ready.
What you should see

Restoring creates a new draft revision and clears its validation. Queries continue using walkthrough-v1 until another published version is activated.

The capture stops immediately after creating the new draft. It does not create or activate a second release.

Files and checkpoints

The guide folder includes the exact demonstration inputs and a published consumer package.

  • power-business-notes.md — upload this business note.
  • reference.sql — independent calculation for the selected metric.
  • walkthrough-v1.consumer.json — exported manifest, Ossie document, context, and artifact bundle.
  • screenshots/ — all original captures.

If a control is disabled

ControlWhat to check
Generate with LLM / Apply to draftSave pending edits. Confirm the provider is configured. Apply a candidate generated for the current revision.
Validate SQLSave the draft first. Every metric needs independent reference SQL before validation can pass.
Approve whole versionValidate the current revision and approve every required review object. Clear review filters to find remaining objects.
Use for queriesPublish the reviewed version first.
Run exampleActivate a published version and reload Data query to obtain its current binding.

Typing a descriptive inclusion rule does not create an executable filter. Inspect the metric expression or structured filters.

Only one linked note is supplied in this power demonstration. Source documents and ontology mappings retain explicit provenance and review status.

Export is a handoff package. Consumer applications still need their integration adapters; local publication does not deploy to another application.
